**Test image observations:** A severely desiccated, brown-to-dark brown mango leaf, completely dried and shriveled/curled. No green tissue visible. No white powdery coating, no black sooty deposits, no discrete lesion spots — the entire leaf appears dead/necrotic and dried out. This is consistent with dieback (tip/shoot dieback leading to complete leaf death) rather than a foliar spot disease.

Now one reference per class:
Strong match — Die_Back reference shows the same completely desiccated, shriveled, brown-dead leaf with similar curled/twisted shape. Now check the other three classes:
Anthracnose reference shows a yellowing/browning leaf with discrete necrotic lesions — different from the test image's fully desiccated form. Now Powdery_Mildew and Sooty_Mould:

Powdery_Mildew: green leaf with white powdery patches — completely unlike the test image. The Die_Back class is clearly the best match. I've now used all 4 views across all 4 classes.

**Summary:**
- **Die_Back**: Perfect match — completely brown, desiccated, shriveled/curled dead leaf with no living tissue
- **Anthracnose**: Partially yellowed/browned leaf with discrete necrotic spots — not matching
- **Powdery_Mildew**: Green leaf with white powdery coating — not matching
- **Sooty_Mould** (inferred): Would show black sooty deposits on green/living tissue — not matching
